addictionPotential: may produce dependence with long-term use; withdrawal syndrome is rare but can be severe including delirium and neuroleptic malignant syndrome
toxicities: Doses over 2g may be fatal. Cardiac toxicity, renal failure, peripheral edema, leukopenia, neutropenia. Accumulates in patients with renal dysfunction.
summary: Amantadine is an adamantane-class dissociative and weak stimulant. It was originally developed as an antiviral for influenza and later found to have dopaminergic effects for Parkinson's disease. At higher doses it produces long-lasting dissociative and deliriant effects.
effectsSummary: Stimulation, euphoria, dissociation, derealization, depersonalization, visual distortions, delirium at high doses, increased heart rate, dry mouth, pupil dilation, nausea, headache.
dosageRemark: Very long duration (12-48 hours). High doses can cause life-threatening cardiac complications. Strongly recommended to use harm reduction practices.
generalRisks: Arrhythmia, dizziness, dry mouth, headache, hyperthermia, tachycardia, nausea, motor control loss, seizures. Delirium at very high doses (>1000mg).
longtermRisks: May cause dependence with withdrawal syndrome. Renal function must be monitored. Cardiac complications with prolonged high-dose use. Cross-tolerance with all dissociatives.
saferUse: Monitor heart rate and blood pressure
Do not combine with other deliriants or stimulants
Avoid if you have renal dysfunction
